quickAnswer: In the US commercial market, a complete two-to-three-phase post-construction office cleanup (Rough Clean + Final Detail Clean + Touch-Up Puff Clean) costs $0.30 to $0.85 per square foot combined, or $55 to $95 per specialty technician hour, with minimum project mobilization fees of $350 to $750. Standalone Phase 1 rough debris and framing sweeps run $0.12 to $0.25 per sq ft, Phase 2 final detail cleaning runs $0.18 to $0.42 per sq ft, and Phase 3 move-in puff cleans add $0.08 to $0.18 per sq ft.

blocks.text: Post-Construction Office Cleanup Unit Prices vs. Recurring Janitorial Rates

Corporate tenant improvement (TI) project managers and office directors frequently experience sticker shock when comparing a post-construction cleanup quote against their ongoing janitorial retainer. While routine commercial office cleaning costs $0.05 to $0.20 per square foot per visit (at standard labor rates of $35 to $65 per hour and ISSA production speeds of 3,500 square feet per hour), a post-construction turnover deals with invasive gypsum drywall dust, silicone caulk smears, manufacturer window labels, paint overspray, and HVAC plenum fallout.

Because sub-micron drywall and masonry silica particles remain suspended in the air column for 48 to 72 hours after general contractors finish sanding and balancing the air handlers, a single pass never leaves a suite move-in ready. Professional commercial bids therefore divide the post-construction office cleanup unit price into three distinct operational phases—or bundle them under a unified per-square-foot turnkey contract—governed by specialty labor rates of $55 to $95 per hour.

blocks.text: Breaking Down the 3 Phases: Rough Clean, Final Clean, and Touch-Up Puff Clean

General contractors (GCs) working under CSI MasterFormat Division 01 (Section 01 74 23 – Final Cleaning) and corporate tenants leasing turnkey build-outs must clearly define which party pays for each phase. If a tenant hires an independent janitorial firm for only a one-day 'Final Clean' while plumbers, electricians, and low-voltage IT installers are still pulling ceiling tiles, ceiling grid fallout will ruin the desks within four hours.

items: Phase 1 – The Rough Clean ($0.12 to $0.25/sq ft): Executed after drywall taping, mudding, and primer coats conclude, but before final floor coverings or modular workstations are installed. Crews haul out cardboard boxes, cable clippings, and lumber scraps (excluding dumpster rental fees), scrape mortar droplets off concrete slabs, and vacuum drywall dust out of wall tracks so flooring adhesives bond properly.

Phase 2 – The Final Detail Clean ($0.18 to $0.42/sq ft): Scheduled once flooring, millwork, glass conference storefronts, and restroom plumbing fixtures are 100% installed. This is the heaviest labor stage: technicians vacuum exposed ceiling ducts and light troffers from top to bottom, razor-scrape manufacturer stickers and silicone glaze off interior glass partitions, wipe inside every breakroom drawer and hinges, sanitize porcelain fixtures, and machine-scrub hard floors.

Phase 3 – The Puff / White-Glove Clean ($0.08 to $0.18/sq ft): Performed 48 to 72 hours after Phase 2—ideally after the punch-list painters and furniture installers vacate. Crews use damp split-microfiber cloths to capture the final veil of fine gypsum dust that settled out of the HVAC air stream.

blocks.text: How Flooring Multipliers and Fixture Density Impact Unit Pricing

Just as ongoing office cleaning applies surface difficulty multipliers to base rates, post-construction estimators adjust their per-square-foot unit prices based on architectural finishes and millwork complexity. An open-concept 15,000-square-foot tech office with sealed polished concrete floors (0.95x flooring multiplier in recurring maintenance) and minimal perimeter drywall cleans up 25% faster than a traditional law office packed with 45 glass-front private offices, crown molding, and stone restrooms.

Ceramic tile and grout restrooms carry a 1.12x labor multiplier in standard cleaning, which jumps even higher during post-construction because grouting haze and thin-set residue require acidic or peroxide-based agitation before sealing. Similarly, newly laid VCT/LVT vinyl floors (1.04x multiplier) often require initial factory-mill-finish scrubbing and two to four coats of commercial polymer finish ($0.18 to $0.35 per square foot extra), whereas engineered hardwood (1.08x multiplier) demands ultra-low-moisture microfiber passes to prevent board cupping while lifting adhesive smudges.

blocks.title: Per-Fixture & Per-Partition Unit Add-On Benchmarks
blocks.text: When estimators price complex office build-outs by component rather than flat square footage, benchmark their line items against these US averages: $25 to $45 per restroom plumbing fixture (toilet, urinal, vanity sink); $8 to $16 per full-height interior glass storefront panel (both sides including sticker/silicone removal); $75 to $160 per breakroom/kitchenette cabinet bank (interior & exterior millwork); and $4 to $8 per 2x4 recessed LED ceiling troffer.
Essential Commercial Tools for Final Detail & Punch-List Turnover

Drywall joint compound dust is alkaline, highly abrasive, and fine enough (2 to 10 microns) to pass straight through standard cloth vacuum bags and redeposit across freshly wiped conference tables. Furthermore, wet-mopping heavy gypsum dust without thorough dry capture turns the powder into chalky gray streaks across carpet edges and grout joints.

To achieve a zero-haze final turnover and protect new occupancy zones during punch-list walkthroughs, top commercial crews pair HEPA filtration vacuums with specialized detailing equipment. During Phase 2 and Phase 3 damp wiping, technicians deploy Rubbermaid Commercial HYGEN Microfiber Damp/Wet Cloths (12-Pack, 16x16-inch split-microfiber rated for 500 commercial launderings, bleach-safe, and color-coded to prevent restroom-to-breakroom transfer), rinsing or swapping folded quadrants every 40 square feet so silica grit never scratches millwork. Whenever auto-scrubbers or neutral damp mops operate across newly finished corridors while GC punch-list trades are still walking the floor, OSHA/ANSI slip-and-fall compliance requires staging the Rubbermaid Commercial 36-Inch Yellow Caution Wet Floor Cone (4-Side bilingual English/Spanish high-visibility stackable barrier) at every corridor intersection. Finally, once executives begin occupying completed wings while minor punch-list adjustments continue nearby, day porters use the whisper-quiet Rubbermaid Commercial 421588 Executive Floor Sweeper (6.5-inch path with soft rubber blades and protective bumper guard) to capture tracked debris in conference rooms during business hours without vacuum motor noise.
How to Transition from Post-Construction Cleanup to Recurring Janitorial Service

The smartest procurement move an office manager can make during a tenant improvement project is awarding the Phase 2/Phase 3 post-construction cleanup to the same janitorial contractor bidding on the ongoing 12-month maintenance agreement. Follow these four steps to leverage your ongoing contract and reduce upfront construction cleanup costs by 15% to 25%:

items.name: Step 1: Verify whether the General Contractor's Bid Includes Phase 1 & Phase 2
items.text: Inspect the GC's Division 01 budget line item. Most commercial GCs include a broom-clean Phase 1 and a basic Phase 2 clean, but exclude Phase 3 white-glove furniture and IT desk detailing.

items.name: Step 2: Bundle Phase 3 Puff Cleaning with Your Recurring Nightly Retainer
items.text: Offer bidding janitorial vendors a 12-month recurring contract (e.g., 3x/week or 5x/week at $0.05–$0.15/sq ft) in exchange for discounting the pre-move-in Final/Puff clean by 20% to 30%.

items.name: Step 3: Require MERV-13 HVAC Filter Changes Before Final Microfiber Detailing
items.text: Never authorize Phase 2 or Phase 3 detailing until the mechanical contractor replaces temporary construction return-air filters; otherwise, dirty ductwork will recoat the office within 24 hours.

items.name: Step 4: Conduct a Daylight Led-Flashlight Inspection Prior to Sign-Off
items.text: Walk interior glass partitions, high door frames, and breakroom upper cabinet shelves at an oblique angle under full daylight before releasing final retention payment.

faqs.q: Why does post-construction office cleaning cost $0.35 to $0.85/sq ft when normal office cleaning is $0.07 to $0.15/sq ft?
faqs.a: Normal nightly janitorial maintenance assumes an already clean baseline where a technician covers 3,500 sq ft per hour emptying trash, spot-wiping desks, and vacuuming traffic lanes. Post-construction cleaning averages only 300 to 600 sq ft per hour net because technicians must clean vertical walls, ceiling grids, cabinet interiors, razor-scrape glass adhesives, and extract heavy gypsum silica dust across two or three separate visits.

faqs.q: Who pays for dumpster rental and construction debris hauling during a rough clean?
faqs.a: Under standard commercial construction contracts, the General Contractor supplies the roll-off dumpster and pays municipal tonnage disposal fees. The post-construction cleaning crew's $0.12–$0.25/sq ft rough-clean price covers labor to consolidate and bag small job-site debris and place it into the GC's on-site container. If the cleaning vendor must haul debris off-site in their own trucks, expect a $350 to $900 dump-fee surcharge.

faqs.q: How do OSHA silica dust rules affect commercial post-construction office cleanup quotes?
faqs.a: Under OSHA's Respirable Crystalline Silica standard (29 CFR 1926.1153), dry sweeping or using compressed air on concrete and masonry dust that can become airborne is restricted. Reputable contractors use true HEPA-filtered commercial vacuums and wet-suppression microfiber techniques, which increases equipment depreciation and filter costs compared to residential-grade broom crews.

faqs.q: What is the minimum service charge for a small office renovation post-construction clean?
faqs.a: Even for a small 800-square-foot conference room remodel or executive suite refresh where standard per-visit janitorial minimums are $90 to $135, specialty post-construction crews typically enforce a $350 to $650 project minimum to cover multi-person team dispatch, HEPA extractors, and two-stage dust settling visits.
